regime_context: The Canada/TSX detector shows a broad eligible rotation (8/16 themes) with Oil & Gas Producers as the dominant leader (score 1.61, 0.79 breadth, durability 0.68) and Gold Miners as the challenger. The absolute-trend gate is validated as risk control on this market's history, but the track record shows directional accuracy of only 0.343 over 99 calls — the detector reliably trims drawdowns but does not reliably pick winners, so leans must stay modest and conditional.
emerging_watch: Watch for a CONFIRMED handoff from Oil & Gas Producers to Gold Miners: I would retire the Oil & Gas overweight read if Gold Miners closes above Oil & Gas in score for 5 consecutive sessions while Gold breadth expands above 0.5 — that would be the observable proof of a real leadership change, not a predicted one.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas Producers present the cleanest trend-gate case: eligible, high durability (0.68, tied for top among eligible names), broad breadth (0.786 — the strongest leader-cohesion reading in the book), and the trend-gate is the only validated edge on this market's history. Crowding (z 1.04) is a size-down caution, not a fade. My medium (not high) conviction reflects the 0.343 directional hit rate: I trust this as a stay-in/avoid-shake-out lean more than a return forecast.
evidence: durability_bar 0.68, breadth 0.786 (highest breadth among all themes)
hurst_tag mixed — not mean-revert, so no reversion flag against the gate
crowded=true (z 1.04) — size-down caution only, per guardrails
theses.dissent: The crowding flag plus a 'mixed' Hurst tag means the regime is not a clean trend; rank-IC is ~0, so today's leadership says nothing about forward return, and an energy commodity reversal would hit this hardest given its weight (0.25 headline).

falsifier.text: XEG.TO closes below its 50-day moving average while Gold Miners (XGD.TO) simultaneously closes above its own 50-day, by the check-by date.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners are the rotation challenger (score 1.11, second-highest), eligible under the trend gate, and NOT crowded (z 0.2) — a differentiated second leg to the energy-heavy leader. But breadth is thin (0.267) and durability moderate (0.48), so this is a weak, conditional lean rather than a confirmed handoff. I lean it only as a diversifying overweight, not a leader replacement.
evidence: rotation.challenger id ca_gold, margin 0.502 from leader
theses.dissent: Breadth 0.267 means the move is narrow and fragile; mean-revert-adjacent durability (0.48, hurst mixed) suggests the trend could stall or reverse quickly, and there is no validated rotation-timing edge to trust the handoff.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms XEG.TO by 8% over the horizon and Gold Miners drops out of the top-3 eligible ranks.

theses.subject: Uranium & Nuclear
theses.thesis: Uranium & Nuclear is the weakest theme in the book (score -1.555, rank 16/16), ineligible under the absolute-trend gate, with near-zero durability (0.14) and zero breadth. Under the validated risk-control lens, this is exactly what the gate is designed to keep you out of. Note it is unscorable (no ETF proxy), so this avoid is a no-position statement rather than a short.
theses.dissent: Mean-reverting or contrarian energy snap-backs occasionally reward early entry into beaten-down themes, and a macro-driven uranium supply shock would not be captured by trend-ranking — but the detector offers no validated edge for that call.

falsifier.text: Uranium & Nuclear theme becomes eligible (trend-gate turns true) and re-enters the top half of ranks without any new trend violation.

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable
